title: Injectivity of an Ext group along injective module maps forces a splitting of the truncation triangle
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an object K of D^-(R), and an integer a, assumes that for every injective R-module map M -> M' the map Ext^{-a}_R(K, M) -> Ext^{-a}_R(K, M') is injective, and concludes that there is a unique direct sum decomposition K = tau_{<= a}K oplus tau_{>= a+1}K with tau_{>= a+1}K of projective-amplitude in [a+1, b] for some b (source lines 19917-19926). The proof starts from the truncation distinguished triangle for K and computes the two Ext groups of tau_{<= a}K: it observes that Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = Hom_R(H^a(K), M) and that Ext^{-a-1}_R(tau_{<= a}K, M) = 0, so the long exact sequence of Ext yields a short exact sequence 0 -> Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) -> Ext^{-a}_R(K, M) -> Hom_R(H^a(K), M), functorial in M (proof lines 19928-19947). The substantive step is the vanishing: for an injective module I one has Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, I) = 0, and since every module injects into an injective module the hypothesis forces Ext^{-a}_R(tau_{>= a+1}K, M) = 0 for every R-module M; the projective-amplitude lemma then gives that tau_{>= a+1}K has projective-amplitude in [a+1, b] for some b, which is where boundedness above is used (proof lines 19948-19956). The splitting then follows from the unique-splitting lemma (proof lines 19956-19957). The non-routine content is the computation of the two Ext groups of the lower truncation and the passage from the vanishing at injective modules to all modules.
